items.title: One server-assembled run context for Do, Plan and scheduled runs: instruction stack, thread history, persona, memory and run notes
items.summary: Extract the ADR-0003 resolver (platform, org, Space, persona, summoned agent) that Ask turns already use into one shared function, add the missing fields to RunAgentRequest, and seed every Do, Plan and scheduled run with the resolved instructions, prior thread turns under the compaction budget, memory prefetch and attachments, with completeness flags on the run record. Automations later get a per-schedule notes block.
items.whyItMatters: Three consolidators found the same defect from different angles (runtime, extensibility, memory): the governed agent loop starts from a preamble plus the goal, so org policy, Space instructions, persona and memory are silently ignored exactly where the agent can take actions. Every reference agent inherits its conversation and instructions. It is the cheapest high-impact fix in the audit and it is a governance gap, not only a quality gap.

items.title: Durable agent loop: checkpoint every round and pause, resume in place after approval, answer or crash, close dangling tool calls, effect ledger
items.summary: Persist the Do loop's fold inputs in session-core at every round and before each effectful call, and add a continuation worker that re-enters the loop at the checkpoint when an approval, a clarifying answer or a crash recovery arrives, instead of re-executing three whitelisted effects from a cold descriptor. Close tool calls that never returned with typed closers, record effects in an exactly-once ledger, park turns whose providers are exhausted, and replay open interaction requests on reconnect.
items.whyItMatters: Today the LLM loop does not resume reasoning after an approval: only execute_provider_action, book_shipment and tickets.create are re-run from a descriptor. That makes every approval a dead end for multi-step tasks and blocks plan-continue, ask_user, scheduled runs with approvals, goals and the computer-use loop. Five of twelve references have durable resume; DeepSeek and Hermes show the exact mechanism.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: DeepSeek (checkpoint before model requests, tool effects and next steps; cold resume repairs the log tail) ; Hermes Agent
others: Hermes (refreshed turn lease with stall watchdog; about 30 failover reasons with a parked-turn countdown)
Cursor (auto-continue of interrupted agents, durable question delivery)
Manus (action ledger keyed by sessionUid and actionId with payload digest and replay horizon; only source)
Claude Desktop, Codex (visible reconnect, per-step model switch)

items.title: Declared tool side-effect classes, a never-auto set and per-tool allow/ask/never policy, so MCP tools become callable through the signed gate
items.summary: Replace the substring classifier is_risky_tool with a declared SideEffectClass (read, read_sensitive, local_mutation, open_world_mutation, external_effect) bound in capability-core's trusted map for every built-in, provider action and discovered MCP tool (unknown defaults to external_effect), add a non-delegable never-auto set, and expose per-connector and per-tool allow/ask/never policy. With registry-owned capability bindings, MCP tools stop being refused by the gate and become usable in Do and, read-only, in Ask.
items.whyItMatters: The model cannot call any MCP tool today (plain chat strips mcp__ names; Do mode offers them but trusted_capability_id returns None so the gate refuses). MCP is table-stakes (6 of 12) and per-tool policy is the standard way references keep it safe. The substring classifier is also the weakest link in an otherwise strong signed-gate design: risk should be declared data, not guessed from names.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (MCP runtime: supervision and recovery, SRC) plus Perplexity web (per-tool allow/ask/never with thread grants, DOC) ; Manus (five declared side-effect levels plus MCP annotations drive policy) for the taxonomy; ChatGPT (graduated Always ask / read / low-risk / all app permissions) with Claude (per-connector never-allow set, Microsoft 365 write-path throttles) for connector policy

items.title: Approvals v2: scoped decisions, typed cause codes, decision provenance, denial memory and step-up for high-risk effects
items.summary: Extend the approval decision from approve/reject to once, this run, this thread or always-as-a-reviewed-rule (an 'always' on a card is held at session scope until confirmed in settings), remember denials within a run, and compute a typed ApprovalCause at the point each permission, hook, capability or browser-risk decision is made. Carry {actor, verdict, cause, rule_id} in the approval event, the durable run log and audit, render a plain localised reason on every card, and require step-up for never-auto or high-risk effects.
items.whyItMatters: Approvals are already durable and stronger than most references (encrypted exact-effect descriptors, postcondition re-checks), but the cards say only that a tool requires approval and every decision is single-use, which produces approval fatigue and teaches users to click through. Codex, Claude and Antigravity show scoped decisions and typed causes as the fix.

items.title: Govern and prove the skill-learning loop: learned skills start as owner-scoped proposals, a seeded eval proves the loop, and a learning ledger supports undo
items.summary: Make every skill written by the background review a proposal owned by the user whose run produced it and not matchable by anyone else, with a Settings > Learning inbox (diff, reason, source run); promotion to org scope needs an admin decision. Then prove the loop end to end with a seeded eval (a real Do run authors a skill a later turn uses) and cost controls, and project memory and skill lineage into a 'What Verevon learned' ledger with undo and rollback.
items.whyItMatters: The learning loop runs by default and its candidates become org-wide matchable skills with no review, owner or scope. That is a data-governance risk (one user's run can change every colleague's agent) as well as a quality risk, and the loop has never been shown to produce a useful skill. Hermes, the reference for self-improvement, stages writes fail-closed and keeps a reversible ledger; Manus emits proposals.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: manus (proposal events); hermes (fail-closed staging) ; hermes ; hermes
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-08-04: 4 of 12 sources (common). | R-t3-08-03: 2 of 12 sources (differentiator). | R-t3-10-06: 1 of 12 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Manus records each learning proposal as a KnowledgeEvent {CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE, PENDING/ACCEPTED/REJECTED, trigger, session_uid, session_event_uid} linked to the session event that produced it, and accepted items can later be enabled or disabled. Hermes forks a background review after the reply is delivered: only if a final response exists and the turn was not interrupted or unattended, it reviews a snapshot of the messages on a cheap model with whitelisted tools (memory, skill_manage) and read-before-write, capped at 16 iterations, with three prompt variants. A JSONL mutation ledger with a row per change {actor, entity, before_hash, after_hash, run_id};

items.title: Agent browser in chat and Do mode on real broker grants, with per-site read/act consent, admin allow/block lists and model-blind logins
items.summary: Replace the placeholder grant id 'session:{id}' with a real browser-broker grant minted per run, whose AllowedDomains come from a per-user site table (control, read only, no access) intersected with admin allow/block lists and the Space decision (block wins). Then expose browser_agent to the model in web-enabled chat and Do mode as a browser subagent with its own profile, budget and recording reference, add a read-only browsing objective usable from Ask and as a deep-research fallback, per-action state diffs, and secret substitution so logins never reach the model.

items.summary: Add a SandboxBackend trait to sandbox-manager (leases already carry backend_id and endpoint) with bwrap as implementation 1 and a microVM backend (Firecracker or Kata, or one attested managed provider) as implementation 2 that stops when idle and snapshots to encrypted object storage. Extend the CAS workspace from Space scope to thread scope, define a typed executor protocol (the cloud loop proposes, the host executes), expose lifecycle states, typed failure causes and a heartbeat in the UI, and harden path handling.
items.whyItMatters: Every 'do the work' reference (Manus, ChatGPT agent, claude.ai, Perplexity) gives each task its own computer; Verevon runs hermetic per-call bwrap processes inside the execution-core container that cannot install tools, keep state or host a browser or desktop. items.title: Make Spaces the chat project: instructions, knowledge, members and a retrieval indicator in Ask and Do
items.summary: Replace the browser-only localStorage project organiser with Space-backed projects. A Space already carries governed instructions, Data Plane v2 knowledge and members, so add a project picker and folder view to the chat sidebar, apply Space instructions and retrieval scope in Do runs as well as Ask, and show a knowledge-mode indicator (in context versus retrieval). Also confirm and expose the multi-author Space room threads that session-core already stores.
items.whyItMatters: Projects are how every comparable product organises ongoing work (7 of 12 sources) and, for Verevon, they are the container that carries org governance: who sees what and which knowledge a run may retrieve. Today chat projects do not survive a browser change and Do runs ignore Space-authored instructions, so the vision of project-scoped agents is visibly missing.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (SRC) plus Claude desktop (SRC) and claude.ai (DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 7 of 12 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A project entity holds versioned, restorable instructions, files and links, default connectors and skills, members with read/write/full roles and a visibility policy (Manus ProjectService, 37 RPCs). Threads carry project_id and inherit that configuration. Knowledge stays in context while it fits and switches to a retrieval tool when it outgrows the window, with a visible indicator (Claude, claude.ai). Real-time multi-user use (C-031) is DOC-only: Manus lets up to 49 collaborators instruct one task, Perplexity uses head-checked optimistic concurrency.

verevonToday.gap: Chat projects are a client-only organiser (max 100) with no instructions, files, memory or sharing. The server container is Spaces, whose instructions are layered into Ask turns but not Do runs, and chat shows no knowledge-mode indicator. session-core already persists space_id, audience refs and a per-message author_subject_id (SRC, migrations 0023/0035), which suggests multi-author Space room threads exist at the data layer, but whether the Application Plane or SPA exposes them as a shared agent thread was not verified.

items.approach: Do not invent a new container. Application Plane keeps Space membership and projections; Data Plane v2 keeps knowledge and the retrieval scope; Model Plane reads Space instructions and scope for both Ask and Do (close the known Do-run instruction-layering gap). SPA: migrate the local organiser into server-synced Space folders (plan I21), add a project picker to the chat sidebar and composer, and render a knowledge-mode badge from the existing retrieval_notice event. First step for the collaboration facet: read the Space room implementation and the author_subject_id read path and write down which actor's delegated token runs a collaborator-triggered agent turn.
dependencies: ADR: Spaces as the chat project container (OD19)
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (membership, projections) with Model Plane (instruction and scope layering) and Data Plane v2 (knowledge)
items.risks: Space access must never widen an owner-plane ACL. Per-member overrides complicate audit. Authority confusion when a collaborator instructs the agent (whose delegated token runs). ChatGPT retired group chats in July 2026 (DOC), a warning that multi-user chat is hard to make useful, so keep collaboration a later phase.

items.title: Content-safety hardening: an injection normaliser, enforcing semantic screening for web and browser content, one policy check on every memory and skill write, and safe links
items.summary: Add a normaliser before scan_injection (NFKC, strip tag-block and zero-width characters, confusable folding, neutralise forged envelope tags), promote the semantic ContentSafety pass from shadow to enforcing for ExternalWeb and Browser trust classes after a false-positive eval, run one deterministic memory policy (identifiers, account and card numbers, credentials, special-category data) on every memory write path including manual and imported memory, govern skill writes, and add safe-link handling and safety UX.
items.whyItMatters: Trust-class provenance and a fail-closed scan are already ahead of most references, but the scanner is evadable by Unicode tricks and memory writes outside the extractor bypass the sensitive-data rule. As browser and connector reads arrive (F-t3-008, F-t3-010) injection exposure grows sharply. Perplexity's layered stack and Claude's homoglyph-aware scrubber are the references.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Perplexity (most layered documented stack: intent anchoring, screening classifier, containment, runtime monitoring) and Claude (homoglyph-aware scrubber neutralising forged envelope tags) for injection; Hermes for memory and skill write governance (staged entry-pinned writes, review fork limited to an allowlist, install-scan trust matrix) ; claude (import flow); web-claudeai (sensitive policy); hermes (write-tool mechanics)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-11-07: injection defences 8 of 12 (table-stakes); skill supply chain 5 of 12; moderation UX 4 of 12; memory write governance 2 of 12 | R-t3-08-06: Import: 5 of 12 (common). items.title: Trajectory ledger with exact model-visible request capture and timing waterfall
items.summary: Add a complete second view of every run next to the chat: a virtualised, grouped ledger (turn, step, request, tool call, sub-call) with a per-record inspector (raw record, payload, result, tool schema, request options, system prompt in effect, usage, timing) and an Inspect action on each chat tool card. Back it with request_snapshot events written at the model call site (parameters, adapter defaults, content-addressed system-prompt and tool-catalogue blobs, auxiliary calls labelled by purpose) and step-level timing events drawn as a waterfall that shows 'unavailable' instead of estimates.
items.whyItMatters: DeepSeek's 'maximum information, very transparent' is an explicit Verevon reference, and long Do-mode and browser runs cannot be explained from a flat event list. This is the strongest single transparency gap: users, support and engineers cannot see what the model was actually sent, which also blocks replay tests (R-t3-10-11) and trustworthy audit.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: deepseek
others: antigravity (DEBUG/FULL verbosity stream, queue and hook/approval time in timing)
t3code (native and canonical provider streams logged side by side)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Ledger: 2 of 12 (differentiator); request capture: 4 of 12 (common); timing waterfall: 3 of 12 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: DeepSeek keeps the invariant 'model-visible implies logged': one append-only per-session log; a request header event {config, adapterDefaults, tools} is appended only when it differs from the previous one; the system prompt is a diffable event; auxiliary requests are logged before dispatch. The ledger is a projection grouped by turn, step and request with request numbers and cumulative usage, 13 inspector tabs, and an Inspect action on each chat tool card. The waterfall is drawn from recorded timestamps only, with time-to-first-token split from decoding and in-flight records showing only a start marker.

verevonToday.gap: The Trace tab is a flat durable run-event list capped at 5,000 with proof and receipts. There is no turn/step/request grouping, no inspector tabs, no Inspect link from a tool card. The context inspector (GET /v1/threads/:id/context, GetContextAssembly) shows assembled segments and token counts, but no per-request snapshot of effective parameters, the exact system prompt or the tool catalogue is persisted or served, and auxiliary calls (title, follow-ups, verification pass) are not shown as requests. Timing is per turn (turn_timing phases plus provider intervals), not per step or tool; no copyable trace/request id was found in the chat UI (INF from grep).

items.approach: Deliver in three slices. (1) Projection and UI: session-core exposes GET /v1/runs/:id/trajectory that groups stored events by turn, step and request (browser actions grouped by action_id); verevonv3 upgrades the Trace tab to a virtualised grouped ledger with an inspector drawer, and tool-presentation carries the event id so tool cards get Inspect. (2) Request capture: at the model-gateway/execution-core call site write request_snapshot events to session-core (provider, model, effort, params, adapter default flags, tool schema list) only when changed, with system prompt and tool catalogue stored as hash-addressed blobs in MinIO (deduplicated), and purpose-labelled auxiliary calls; under ZDR persist only hashes and parameter metadata and render 'not retained (ZDR)'. Decide which Verevon persona/policy prompt text is shown versus hashed. (3) Timing: emit step_timing {step_id, queued_at, started_at, first_token_at, ended_at} from the existing OTEL spans (including approval wait and hooks), expose trace id on usage, draw the waterfall strip, add a copy-trace-id action. Owner-only access as today; never widen Space ACLs.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (session-core, model-gateway, execution-core) and Frontend Plane (Trace tab)
items.risks: Prompt and payload tabs can expose tenant secrets or other users' content in shared Spaces, so they stay owner-only with redaction and no ACL widening; ZDR must propagate (no prompt content persisted); persona/policy prompt IP visibility needs a decision; storage growth and virtualisation for very large runs; clock skew across services must never be papered over by synthesised timings.

items.title: Wide research: user entry point, honest estimate and spend gate, per-item retry, replay after reload
items.summary: Give the existing subagent.research_fan_out engine a product surface. Add a 'Bred forskning' control with item-count presets, a start card that states the expected scale before anything is spawned (items x rounds x minutes, plus cost on metered routes), a status grid of per-item cards with retry for failed or refused items, a mid-run progress and spend check after the first N items (Continue or Wrap up now), and durable per-item results so the grid survives a reload. Under ZDR the grid stays live-only.
items.whyItMatters: Wide research is Manus's signature feature and serves Verevon's B2B lists (suppliers, competitors, leads). The engine is already paid for; without an entry point, a cost statement and retry it is unusable and unsafe, and a cost gate fits Verevon's honest-cost stance.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (manus-product-ux-038 SRC UX, web-manus-web-product-023 DOC architecture)
others: Manus web (DOC): plan limits on concurrency and task count
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 11 sources (both Manus); differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Controller decomposes into independent items -> estimate a cost range from per-item budget x item count -> start card with Start or 'Always auto-start' -> spawn up to K concurrent isolated sub-runs, each in its own context -> stream per-item status into a 3-column grid with replay link and retry -> after the first N items compute actual spend and show a Skip or Continue card -> 'Wrap up now' -> controller merges structured per-item results. Sub-agents never talk to each other.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: engine exists (one tool call, N parallel items, structured per-item results merged in order, kill switch WIDE_RESEARCH_FAN_OUT_ENABLED, default concurrency 4) and live cards by batchId exist. Missing: a composer entry point (planned C6), a pre-run estimate and accept gate, a mid-run spend check, per-item retry, durable replay (cards come back empty after reload, planned C7), and scale (default 4 rounds and 2 subagents on the subscription route; 12/24/48 presets wait on owner decision OD7). Do mode only. DOC: on the subscription route cost-core meters nothing (CostBasis::Subscription), so a USD budget is a no-op there.

items.approach: Model Plane execution-core: add an estimate step before spawning that is computed from item count, round budget and observed per-item p50 time, and expressed in items, rounds and minutes (USD only when the route is metered, via a run-scoped cost-core check such as the planned cost_guard.rs). Emit an awaiting-approval style start card that the user can set to 'always auto-start', and after the first N completed items emit a progress and spend card with Continue or Wrap up now. Persist the batch and per-item results in session-core so replay works after reload, and add a retry action per item that re-spawns only that child (research-only toolset, C8). Long batches run through the existing WideResearch Temporal workflow (apps/Model Plane/go/services/orchestrator-core/cmd/workflows/wide_research.go). Frontend: 'Bred forskning' control, estimate card, grid with retry, spend card. Under ZDR skip persistence and degrade to a live-only grid.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Spend blowouts and provider rate limits at scale. OD7 recommends no confirm gate in v1; the estimate card should therefore default to informational for small runs and gate only above an org-set size. Credential lifetime caps wide research at about 6 to 8 items on Terra without C9. ZDR forbids durable replay.

items.title: Persistent goals with a token budget, a completion judge and auto-continuation
items.summary: Add a Goal record in session-core {objective, success_criteria, token_budget, used, status active|completed|blocked|cancelled} and a continuation driver, hosted as a Temporal workflow in orchestrator-core, that starts budgeted Do runs until a cheap judge model (verevon-balance) confirms the criteria with evidence, or a budget or blocker is hit, then notifies the user. The Agent Run Console's goal launcher is the natural UI host, with a goal bar showing budget used and compare-and-set edits.
items.whyItMatters: Outcome agents that work for a long time are the core of the Manus and ChatGPT Work vision, and goals are present in 6 of 12 references. Verevon has no goal primitive, and long autonomous work is also capped by the 300 s delegated bearer and a default of 4 rounds, so a user cannot hand over a multi-step objective and come back to a result.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (persisted ThreadGoal with token budget and an audited completion check)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 6 of 12 sources (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Goal{objective, success_criteria, token_budget, used, status}. When the run goes idle, a continuation driver re-prompts with the goal state; a cheap judge checks completion against the criteria with evidence; stop on budget exhaustion or a blocker and notify. Completion is audited, not self-declared by the worker model.

items.title: Sandbox egress tiers and a credential-injecting egress proxy, with per-call enforcement reports and shell-grammar approvals
items.summary: Add an org and user network tier (off, package registries, allowlisted domains, all) stamped on the sandbox lease and mapped to the existing fail-closed MpNetworkPolicy, backed by a deployed egress proxy that injects vaulted credentials so sandboxes only ever see sentinels. Surface the per-call 'sandboxed' result and enforcement level in the Do loop and tool cards, add shell-grammar-aware approvals and versioned file writes.
items.whyItMatters: Sandboxes currently have no network, which blocks package installs and API work; references (claude.ai, Manus) use egress tiers, and Claude's credential masking is the safe way to give sandboxes authenticated access. Verevon's fail-closed proxy design is already strict; it needs deploying and exposing.

items.title: Sharing, replay, export and import: governed snapshot links, org-only default, and conversation export and import
items.summary: Add a session-core snapshot entity (owner, visibility org or named people, created_from_message) whose grants are checked through Control Plane and audited, with public links only behind admin policy and refused for ZDR threads and threads that used private connectors unless redacted. Viewers read it read-only and a follow-up creates a fork under the viewer; a replay view is built from the durable run event log. In parallel add an owner-only audited whole-conversation export and an importer that maps ChatGPT and Claude export JSON into origin=import threads.
items.whyItMatters: Teams share answers and agent runs constantly and org-only sharing is expected in B2B (8 of 12 sources). A replay of an agent run is also a strong trust and transparency artefact. Importing history lowers switching cost, and reports must leave Verevon as Office files and PDFs.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (SRC) for visibility, roles, replay and admin policy; claude.ai and Perplexity (DOC) for snapshot hygiene and fork-on-follow-up; Manus (SRC) and Claude desktop (SRC) for conversion and import

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Share is an immutable snapshot of the thread up to a message (artifacts included, raw tool and connector payloads and files excluded unless in-org) with a visibility enum and an audit entry. Viewers load read-only, a follow-up forks under the viewer, replay plays recorded steps with a countdown and skip-to-result, and admin policy can disable public or replay sharing (strictest wins). Export uses server-side conversion jobs with PENDING, CONVERTING, SUCCESS and FAILED states, session export as a zip (rate-limited, policy-gated), and importers that enumerate sources and can remove an import run.

items.title: Typed run lifecycle events and status cues: retry, turn end, compaction, context-change source chips, thread status, connector incidents
items.summary: Add the missing lifecycle events to the ChatEvent taxonomy and render them: retry_scheduled {attempt, delay_ms, code}, a typed turn_end {reason} (including an explicit 'outcome unknown' result for interrupted tool calls), a compaction marker {items_condensed, tokens_before, tokens_after, summary_ref}, and context_change rows (skill attached, pin, reattach_context, memory recall, trigger kind such as schedule, watcher, webhook, subagent). Derive one thread status with fixed precedence and an unseen-completion dot from the typed end reason, and keep a bounded per-connector incident ring with normalised reasons.
items.whyItMatters: Today retries and compaction happen silently, so users see a stall or a changed context with no explanation, and runs started by schedules or watchers do not say why they started. These are cheap, highly visible trust wins that also give the trajectory ledger (R-t3-10-03) its rows.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: deepseek
others: hermes (hel-018 deterministic 'recalled N memories' line from the host)
t3code (t3u-021 status resolver with precedence, rollup and unseen completion; t3u-053 slow-request toast)

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Retries and end reasons: 1 of 12 (unique); compaction marker: 1 of 12 (unique); message source: 2 of 12 (differentiator); status pills: 1 of 12 (unique); connector incidents: 2 of 12 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: DeepSeek appends a retry event before waiting (honouring Retry-After), writes a terminal turn event with a typed reason (completed, aborted with cause, blocked, error, max-tokens, crash-interrupted, forked), uses stable error codes with cause chains, and synthesises explicit error results for unanswered tool calls so the model re-checks state. Compaction emits a CompactionItem with the shadowed item and token counts plus the summary node. Every persisted message carries a typed source {kind, form, label}; context injections emit host-authored notice events rendered as one-line rows.

verevonToday.gap: SRC (variant list read): the ChatEvent enum has Stopped {reason}, Error {code, message, retryable}, Usage, TurnTiming, MemoryRecall and others, but no retry, compaction or context-change variant, so tool-call retries (up to 3) and compaction are invisible; typed failure presentation and continue-after-stop already exist on the client. Memory recall is disclosed with provenance, but no user-visible source kind per message, no trigger chips for scheduled or watcher runs, and no rows for skill attach, pins or reattach_context were found (skills unknown). Thread history shows run status chips and the Work panel shows 'needs you', but an attention rollup and unseen-completion indicator were not verified. Capability-core has health attestation that fails closed, but no per-connector incident history is visible to users and no slow-request indicator was found.

Under ZDR the compaction summary text must not persist beyond the turn (counts only). Frontend: a collapsed 'waiting to retry' row, a divider marker with expandable summary, a trigger chip on turn headers, and a status resolver (needs you, running, failed, completed-unseen, idle) with sidebar rollup using completedAt versus last-visited. capability-core: bounded incident ring per MCP/integration with a normalised reason taxonomy and redacted stderr tail, shown on the integrations page.

items.title: Make images a governed agent tool: typed generation, an edit endpoint with a mark tool, a second provider, and C2PA provenance
items.summary: Expose image generation to the agent loop as a generate_image tool with a typed result (artifact id, revised prompt, model, transparency, failure), a per-run concurrency limit, a prompt screen and no silent model fallback; add a Gemini image adapter and a newer OpenAI image model behind a provider-neutral contract and a model picker. Add an edit endpoint (mask inpainting, reference images) that writes a new artifact version, with a simple rectangle-and-brush mark tool over the preview that carries a note per region. Sign generated images with C2PA content credentials in the artifact writer.
items.whyItMatters: Image creation is expected in any general assistant (4 of 11 sources, table-stakes) and editing is the normal second step; without it image mode is a dead end. Making generation a tool is what lets reports and decks (R-t3-02-01, -05) include generated visuals. Machine-readable marking of AI-generated media is a governance differentiator for EU B2B buyers.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (SRC) for the typed result and no-silent-fallback rule; Cursor (SRC) for operational guards; Manus (SRC and DOC) for the edit and mark canvas; Claude desktop (SRC) for C2PA
others: Antigravity (SRC, image_paths for edit and combine)
ChatGPT web (DOC, UX bar for region selection)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Generation: 4 of 11, table-stakes (class adjusted). Editing: 4 of 11 (3 distinct vendors), common. C2PA: 1 of 11 with a second DOC mention, unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Tool generate_image{prompt, size or aspect, model?, transparent?, reference_ids?} calls a provider adapter and returns {artifact_id, revised_prompt, model, transparent, failure?}; a per-run semaphore (Cursor uses 2) and a prompt screen run before dispatch; a fallback to a weaker model needs user confirmation. Edit: edit_image{base_artifact_id, reference_ids[], regions[{mask or bbox, instruction}], prompt} calls a provider edit endpoint and creates a new artifact version linked to the base; the canvas draws marks as masks (Manus Konva canvas with Mark tool); upscale and background removal are separate jobs. C2PA: build a manifest (generator, model, timestamp, actions), sign with a service certificate and embed in PNG/JPEG/PDF (Claude desktop ships a Rust/WASM c2pa module).

verevonToday.gap: Generation exists only as a request flag (generate_image) reached through the /image slash command; it takes over the whole turn (SRC sse.rs:1425-1432, DashboardComposer.tsx:477-485), so an agent run cannot create an image for a report. Default model is gpt-image-1 (SRC provider/vision.rs:14); a requested model string is accepted only if it looks like an image model (SRC sse.rs image_generation_model), with no picker and no revised-prompt surfacing; no per-run concurrency limit or prompt screen was found in the sse.rs image path (comparator, confirmed by grep). Never run live and unavailable on the ChatGPT subscription route. No edit or mask endpoint (the image routes are /v1/ai/images, /analyze and /ocr), no reference-image input, no mark UI. No c2pa matches in apps/Model Plane (grep, 2026-10-13).

items.approach: Model Plane: add generate_image to the tool_loop tool list as a new module with a one-line seam (as the plan prescribes for new tools), keep image_gen_stream as the explicit-mode path; typed result and a semaphore and prompt screen in the tool; a provider-neutral adapter in inference-core (Gemini image adapter, newer OpenAI image model) with model choice surfaced to the SPA; POST /v1/ai/images/edit (mask plus references) writing a new artifact version with lineage; C2PA signing in the model-gateway artifact writer using the c2pa crate and a per-deployment certificate held as a Control Plane secret, starting with PNG and JPEG, then PDF and Office through the same writer (signing needs no persistence, so it also works under ZDR). Frontend Plane: model selector and revised-prompt disclosure in image mode; a mark overlay (rectangle and brush producing a mask and a note per region) that the annotation work in R-t3-02-07 reuses; authorship badge from the manifest. Live-prove on the paid route before claiming parity.

items.title: Composer: atomic typed context tokens, per-thread drafts, large attachments through Data Plane, and thread references
items.summary: Turn the composer into a rich editor where references (Data Plane document, past thread, Space, skill) become atomic typed tokens serialised as content parts {type, id}, resolved by model-gateway with the caller's delegated token. Persist drafts per thread (prompt, attachments, tokens) under the existing ZDR purge rules, route large files through Data Plane v2 import instead of inlining them (today 1 MB per file), and let the agent browse referenced threads lazily through read-only outline, search and read tools.
items.whyItMatters: Typed references make context explicit and auditable, which suits Verevon's authority model better than free text. Losing a long prompt on reload is a top frustration, and 1 MB per file is far below every reference for document-heavy business users.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: T3 Code (SRC) for atomic Lexical chips and drafts; Antigravity (SRC) for typed scope items and server slash commands; Manus (SRC/DOC) for task references browsed lazily; Claude desktop and ChatGPT (DOC) for large-paste handling
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 6 of 12 (typed composer, table-stakes), 4 of 12 (attachments), 2 of 12 each (drafts, thread references)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A rich-text editor with decorator nodes per token type; triggers for @, / and $ detected at the cursor; offsets map between collapsed (one char per chip) and expanded forms; the send payload is a list of text and typed scope items; slash commands come from a server endpoint. Drafts persist per thread in versioned localStorage (debounced writes, flush on unload, byte budgets). Long pastes over a threshold become attachments and uploads are validated by type and size (Manus 300 MB). Thread references carry up to 20 task ids whose access is checked lazily at read time, and the agent gets outline, search and read-part tools instead of injected content.

verevonToday.gap: Slash commands (/file, /image, /search, /research, /schedule plus server skills, capabilities and connectors) and an entity overlay ship, but @-mentions are deliberately not handled in the global composer (Space rooms own governed agent mentions), tokens are not atomic typed items in the payload, and user slash templates are absent. The Home draft persists per user and org and is purged under ZDR, but no per-thread chat draft store was found (inference from grep, medium confidence). Attachments cap at 1,000,000 bytes per file, 60,000 characters per file and 120,000 per turn (SRC prepare-chat-attachments.ts:18-35); long paste becomes an attachment at 4,000 characters; there is no image annotation and files are not staged into the code sandbox. No thread references or recall tool exist.

items.approach: SPA: Solid rich-text composer with typed tokens serialised as content parts {type: doc_ref|thread_ref|space_ref, id}; use a different trigger or scoped menu than the Space-agent @ the owner reserved. model-gateway resolves refs with the caller's delegated token (owner-plane ACL check at read time, never widened by Space access) and exposes read-only thread outline, search and read tools that reuse the recall index from R-t3-01-03. Generalise home-draft-storage to a per-thread key with the same ZDR purge and size clamps. Large files go through Data Plane v2 chunked import and retrieval; stage attachments into sandbox workspaces for code_interpreter; raise limits per plan.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (editor, drafts), Model Plane (ref resolution, thread tools, attachment routing), Data Plane v2 (large files)
items.risks: The owner's decision to keep @ for Space agents must be respected. Cross-thread references leak across ZDR boundaries unless ZDR threads are refused. Large files must not persist under ZDR. Referenced thread content is untrusted data.

items.title: Web reading upgrade: chunked long-page reader and a batched, reference-id web tool
items.summary: Stop cutting fetched pages at 4,000 characters. When a page is longer, return an outline plus the first chunk and a reference id, and add read_page(ref, chunk) and find_in_page(ref, query) that work over the cached full text with no new egress. In the same change let web_search take queries:[..] (max 4, deduplicated, concurrent) and return one merged, capped, de-duplicated list with stable reference ids and a standing cite instruction. Keep the SSRF boundary in Quarry, injection screening of the full text before any cut, the relevance gate, and the separate vertical tools.
items.whyItMatters: B2B users research long primary sources (annual reports, regulations, tenders, PDFs) that chat currently cuts at 4,000 characters and deep research reads at 4,000 characters per page. Reference ids make citations exact (the cited page is the page the model opened), and batching cuts tool rounds and latency in Ask-mode research. Fetch safety itself is already ahead of the references.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: DeepSeek harness (deepseek-harness-architecture-081 safe fetch, deepseek-harness-architecture-160 batched search; SRC) for the blueprint; Codex (codexagent-agent-runtime-and-models-084, SRC) for typed operations and reference ids
others: Antigravity (SRC): outline-then-chunk reader (VIEW_CONTENT_CHUNK) and a permission step for non-allowlisted URLs
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 11 sources for batched operations (Codex, DeepSeek) and 2 of 11 for chunked or hardened fetch (Antigravity, DeepSeek); differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Fetch: resolve and vet the host, pin the vetted addresses, stop on cross-origin redirects, decode text-like types, sanitise, convert to bounded markdown labelled untrusted; when long, store the full text, return an outline plus chunk 1 and expose view_chunk(n). Search: validate 1 to 4 non-blank queries, collapse duplicates, run concurrently under one abort signal, interleave round-robin by rank, drop repeated URLs, cap at 8, then format title-url-snippet lines with an untrusted-content prefix and a closing instruction to cite these URLs. Results get stable reference ids so open, click and find act on an id, not a raw URL.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: web_search takes one query per call (query, intent, limit); multi-query concurrency exists only inside deep research. fetch_url takes a raw URL and truncates at MAX_FETCH_CHARS = 4,000 with no outline or continuation. There are no result reference ids and no open, click, find-in-page or PDF-page operations. SSRF vetting (Quarry dns_guard.rs), full-text injection screening before truncation, and a JS-page escalation to the browser driver are already shipped and ahead of DeepSeek and Antigravity.

items.approach: Model Plane model-gateway. Reuse the existing result-handle store (tool_result_handles.rs, section 23.6: tenant-keyed, 900 s TTL, no handle created under ZDR) with a new text-page kind that supports offset or chunk paging and an outline, instead of building a second cache. fetch_url keeps its current screening (assess_external_payload on the complete text) and, when the body exceeds MAX_FETCH_CHARS, parks the full text and returns the outline, chunk 1 and a handle. Add read_page(handle, chunk) and find_in_page(handle, query) (INF: select_passages in grounding.rs:438 can serve find_in_page and the default chunk). Under ZDR use a turn-scoped in-memory cache dropped at turn end (INF: that is not retention past the turn). web_search accepts queries:[..], fans out to the Quarry client concurrently as deep research already does, merges round-robin, dedupes with the existing canonical URL key, caps, and tags each hit with a reference id used by fetch_url and the citation events. Keep Norwegian vertical tools as separate tools. Pairs with planned F7 (paged file text) so attachments and pages share one paging contract.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Every chunk must keep untrusted provenance and be screened (the handle store notes that untrusted content must be assessed before parking). Handles expire after 900 s and do not exist under ZDR. Wider fan-out raises paid-provider cost, so respect allow_paid_providers and per-org quota. Tool results are re-sent each round, so chunk size must stay bounded.

items.title: Web access governance and provider transparency: org web policy, domain rules, cached-only mode, 'searched via' disclosure
items.summary: Add an org web policy owned by Control Plane (web on or off, allowed and blocked domains for search and fetch, allowed paid providers, cached-only mode, optional provider pin) that capability-core puts in the capability bearer and model-gateway enforces at dispatch for web_search and fetch_url next to the existing source-scope prune, with Quarry re-checking at execution. Make routing visible: Quarry returns its router decision (provider and reason), the Sources panel shows 'Searched via X', and a Settings or Trust page lists each upstream provider, what query data leaves, retention, and crawl behaviour. Per-domain consent for unknown domains is a prompt on Do runs only.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprise admins, Verevon's buyers, need to restrict where agents read from and to see where queries go. A cached-only mode (served from Quarry's own index with no live third-party egress, INF) supports ZDR claims, and visible provider choice matches the transparency goal set by the DeepSeek harness.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude (claude-product-ux-076 and claude-runtime-architecture-004, SRC): org capability switch, per-surface preference, provider or custom URL, per-domain fetch consent with an admin-skippable preflight, egress allow-lists
others: Codex (SRC): disabled, cached or live search modes with location hints
Cursor (SRC): hooks and classifier coverage on web calls
DeepSeek (SRC): named search provider with explicit selection states and per-provider limits
Perplexity and ChatGPT (DOC): published robots.txt and partner-sharing statements
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 3 of 11 sources for governance (Claude, Codex, Cursor); 1 of 11 each for the provider seam (DeepSeek) and data-handling disclosure (Perplexity); differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Capability flag per org and surface, so the tool is offered only when on. Fetch runs a domain preflight, asks the user once per unknown domain (allow once or always), persists the grant, and admins can pre-approve. Web calls pass through the same pre and post tool hooks as shell and MCP. Provider resolution is explicit: configured and available uses it, configured and missing is a typed error, none configured and exactly one usable uses it, else ambiguous. Each provider exports a limits and cost descriptor shown in settings.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: shipped are an explicit per-turn web toggle enforced server-side, source-scope pruning with a source_scope_applied receipt, paid providers gated by tier and retention (allow_paid_providers always serialised), and per-hit provider attribution. Missing: an org-level domain allow or block list for fetch_url and search (include and exclude domains exist only as model-authored per-call options), per-domain user consent, a cached-only mode, admin choice of provider, a visible router decision (Quarry's SmartSearchRouter picks among tantivy_local, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily, Bing and Google and the intent hint is dropped), and any customer-facing statement of crawl policy or upstream data sharing. Domain policy exists only for browser runs (broker grant allowed_domains).

items.approach: Control Plane owns the org web policy setting. capability-core mints it into the capability bearer. model-gateway enforces it where the scope prune already runs and re-checks at dispatch; Quarry-v2 re-validates domain rules on execution (keeps 'Model proposes, Quarry executes'). Cached-only mode restricts SmartSearchRouter to local or self-hosted providers (INF) and blocks live fetches outside the index. Extend the search reply with provider and reason, forward it in the tool_result and grounding events, and render 'Searched via X' in the Sources panel. Unknown-domain consent on Do runs reuses the awaiting_approval HITL card. Publish a Trust page section from a verified provider table (provider, data sent, retention) only after checking it against the actual Quarry behaviour including robots_cache.rs and crawl_denial.rs.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane
items.risks: Per-domain prompts cause approval fatigue, so default to admin policy and prompt only for unknown domains on Do runs. Do not leak provider keys or internal routing heuristics to clients. A published data-handling statement must match real behaviour. Cached-only mode lowers answer freshness, so surface that in the answer.

items.title: Connectors: in-chat suggestion cards with resumable connect, and editable write confirmation with per-tool policy
items.summary: Two parts on top of the connector read path. (a) A suggest_connector built-in tool that returns an opt-in card from the integration-corev2 provider catalogue (reason and use_when) when a task needs an app that is not connected; Connect starts OAuth and stores a connect intent (conversation id and pending step) in the gateway session so the turn resumes after the callback. Never auto-connect, never rank by payment. (b) Classify every provider action read or write in the catalogue (CatalogOp.is_write already exists), add per-tool policy levels (always ask, ask once per session, always allow for reads, blocked) in capability-core, and show an editable preview card for mail drafts and calendar events before the write; the executor applies the confirmed payload exactly.
items.whyItMatters: Suggestion cards cut setup friction and grow connector adoption without breaking the grant model, since the user still completes OAuth. Editable write cards keep the authority model explicit and are the difference between a trusted and a feared 'send on my behalf'.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude (claude-product-ux-077 and -150, claude-product-ux-078, SRC) for suggestion registry, connect intents and four-level tool policy; Manus (SRC) for editable email-draft and calendar-event cards
others: Claude.ai web (DOC): memory-tailored, several options when several fit, no sponsored ranking, never transacts without confirmation
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 11 sources for suggestions (common); 2 of 11 for write policy and cards (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: The model has search_registry and suggest_connectors tools and emits a card (connector id, reason). The connect intent survives the login redirect and the turn continues with the new tool. Each connector tool is pre-classified from read-only and destructive annotations; a per-user or per-org policy store has scopes once, session and persistent; on a write the runtime emits a structured editable preview, the user edits and confirms, and the executor applies exactly the confirmed payload.

Provider writes already exist in execution-core's catalogue as is_write entries (mail.send, gmail.send, message.send, pages.post and others) and run through the Do-mode capability-policy, hook, permission and HITL pipeline with an exact-effect descriptor and postcondition check. items.title: Custom connectors: probe-and-test add flow, a REST/API-key connector kind and a vault-brokered egress proxy
items.summary: Users can register, OAuth-connect, scope and share MCP servers, but cannot probe a server before saving, choose tools from the discovered list, or add a plain REST connector. Add a probe endpoint (initialize, tools/list, auth detection), an API connector kind executed by a server-side egress proxy that injects vaulted secrets and enforces host allow-lists, and a proxy-only network namespace for sandbox code or skills that legitimately need network access.
items.whyItMatters: It lets a business plug in its own ERP, CRM and internal APIs without waiting for first-party connectors (a main reason teams choose Claude or Manus), keeps keys out of model context and sandboxes, and strengthens the ZDR and security story. Custom connectors: 4 of 12 sources; secret brokering: 3 of 12.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (one service validates the server, auto-detects OAuth, inspects tools before save, imports JSON, supports API connectors with secrets, publishes to team or project; SRC) plus Claude desktop (vault-injected credentials with per-operation confirm rules and a network allow-list; SRC)
others: Perplexity web (egress proxy for custom APIs with session, personal and project scopes)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Custom connectors 4 of 12, common; host-brokered secrets 3 of 12, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Add flow: URL -> probe (initialize + tools/list) -> detect auth (401 with WWW-Authenticate or resource metadata) -> OAuth or API-key form -> show discovered tools with per-tool toggles -> save with scope (user | space | org). API connectors are an OpenAPI or header definition executed by a server-side proxy that injects the secret. Vault entries {scope, secret, allowed hosts}; the model and sandbox see only a placeholder; operation rules map request patterns to named operations with confirm or deny.

verevonToday.gap: Register, delete, share, OAuth start/callback and connect routes exist; scope (user or org) and sharing are modelled; MCP OAuth tokens are vaulted. There is no probe or test route, no discovered-tool toggle list, no plain REST/API-key connector type, and no general secret vault with egress-proxy injection for API connectors or sandbox code (the sandbox has no network at all).

items.approach: Model Plane. model-gateway: a probe endpoint reusing the MCP client and its SSRF and DNS guards. capability-core: an api_connector kind with typed operations carrying read/write class, bound under item 01. Egress proxy (Ingestion Plane or a Model Plane egress service) matching host and injecting header or token from the vault, with per-operation confirm rules; sandbox-manager: a proxy-only network namespace for opted-in skills (item 03). SPA: an Inspect/Test step and tool toggles in McpServersSection. Org-scope sharing stays inside the owner ACL (Space access never widens it).
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (with an Ingestion Plane egress service if the proxy lives there)
items.risks: The proxy becomes an exfiltration path if host allow-lists are loose; API connectors need the same SSRF guards as MCP; org-scope sharing must not widen an owner-plane ACL; secrets must never reach logs or traces.

items.title: Plugin manifest loader with supply-chain pins, cross-vendor adapters and an org-curated catalogue
items.summary: Plugins are an inert durable registry today: manifests, risk and rollout state are stored but nothing loads them. Build a loader that expands a plugin into child capabilities at install (skills, URL-only MCP servers, slash commands, agent presets, routine templates, hooks), accepts the open agent-plugins.org manifest and foreign .claude-plugin, .codex-plugin and .cursor-plugin layouts through adapters (reporting unsupported stdio or bin components), pins every source to a commit SHA or archive digest with a kill list, and starts with an org-curated catalogue rather than a public marketplace.
items.whyItMatters: A plugin is the unit by which Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and Cursor distribute capability (7 of 12 sources: table-stakes), and for Verevon it is how a vertical solution (for example shipping ops = provider actions + skills + routines) reaches an org. Building on the open formats gives instant compatibility with users' existing skills and plugins (4 of 12), and supply-chain pins are cheap when designed in from the start.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (plugin manifest with typed userConfig, sha-pinned binaries and many extension points; SRC) plus Codex (open agent-plugins.org 1.0 manifest with foreign-namespace adapters, a capabilities-from-this-plugin prompt block, atomic upgrade with rollback; SRC); Hermes for supply chain (about 570 catalogue entries each pinned to a 40-hex commit, CI that clones every entry, a removed.yaml kill list; SRC)
others: Manus (addons split tools into model-visible and host-callable)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Plugin package 7 of 12, table-stakes; marketplaces 4 of 12, common; cross-vendor compatibility 4 of 12, common; supply-chain safety 3 of 12, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Manifest (agent-plugins.org 1.0 compatible): name, version, skills/, commands/, agents/*.md (model, tool allow/deny, permission mode), mcpServers (URL-only for Verevon), hooks, scheduled-task templates, userConfig schema. Install resolves components into capability entries (a plugin parent with children), prompts for userConfig and vaults secrets; a selected plugin adds a short capabilities block to the prompt. Every source resolves to an immutable digest, install scripts never run, every referenced path must stay inside the package root, names are checked against advisories, and a server-side blocklist is re-evaluated on each load. Upgrade = stage, validate, swap atomically, keep a rollback copy.

verevonToday.gap: A durable per-org plugin registry (manifest JSON, risk level, rollout state, default disabled and unpinned) and the single Capability registry with a Kind discriminator exist, but the handler's own comment says registering a plugin is inert until a host loads its manifest, and nothing does (SRC). No install flow, marketplace or catalogue exists. Whether plugin_packages stores digest or signature fields is unverified. A grep for agent-plugins.org found no code (INF: absent).

items.approach: Model Plane capability-core: a manifest loader that expands a plugin into child capabilities and rejects stdio and bin components; a digest and signature column per plugin version, a refusal of unpinned sources, a central kill list checked at load, and an install review screen that lists every component and its risk with hash-the-declared-set consent. Adapters normalise foreign layouts into the internal model and report unsupported parts instead of dropping them silently. Control Plane owns the org catalogue and publish review; Model Plane resolves and pins entries; Frontend Plane gets the install and enable UI. Start with an org-curated catalogue only.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (capability-core) with Control Plane for the org catalogue and review
items.risks: A plugin aggregates risk: one install can add write tools and hooks at once, so the install must show every component; foreign plugins assume local shell or stdio, which Verevon refuses; supply-chain attacks through catalogue entries and review workload.

items.title: Loop guard, durable org hooks and universal tool-output handles in both loops
items.summary: (1) A LoopGuard in mp-contracts used by both loops: a rolling window of (tool, args hash, result class) with an escalating reminder at 3, 5 and 8 identical failing calls, a stop with a typed loop_detected end reason, a repetition detector for streamed text (code-fence aware) and bounded retry on empty or length-stopped responses. (2) Persist org and Space hook rules in capability-core and pass hook_context into Do runs, which today receive none; handlers stay declarative rules plus HTTP webhooks (no shell) and hooks may only narrow authority. (3) Generalise ToolResultHandle from MCP results to every built-in tool result above a token threshold (fetch_url, knowledge, provider actions), run-scoped and never stored on ZDR turns.
items.whyItMatters: A stuck run that keeps repeating a failing call wastes tokens and is exactly what users describe as "it keeps doing the same thing". Hooks let org admins enforce policy (for example block mail outside the domain) without code changes, and result handles protect the context window in Do runs that read large documents. All three are small wiring jobs on existing primitives.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (side-effect-free loop controller for repeat, cycle and no-progress detection with stop gates) for the guard; Cursor (generic and tool-specific pre/post hooks) for hooks; DeepSeek (private spill files with opaque locators inside a shared token budget) for output handles

Codex (command, MCP-tool and agent hook handlers)

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Guard: rolling window of (tool, args hash, result class); on N identical failing calls or no new information inject an escalating reminder, then stop with a loop reason. Hooks: registry {event, matcher, handler(command|http|prompt), timeout}; pre-hooks return allow|deny|ask plus optional rewritten input and context; durable store with per-org admin rules. Spill: if output exceeds max_inline_tokens store the full text as a run-scoped blob and return {preview_head, marker, preview_tail, handle, size}; a read tool fetches ranges; blobs expire with the run.

items.title: Rewind with undo preview, read-only side chat and spin-off tasks, built on the message tree
items.summary: Once the server message tree exists, add three tree operations. Rewind moves the active leaf to before an earlier message and restores the artifact version pointer, with a preview and an undo of the rewind. Side chat is an ephemeral child thread seeded with a read-only snapshot of the parent's context, with inline read-only tools only, usable while the run continues. Spin-off lets the assistant propose a draft thread chip with a seeded prompt that the user must accept.
items.whyItMatters: Rewind is a differentiator for safe experimentation in Do mode, side chat (6 of 12 sources) lets users ask 'why did it do X?' mid-run without redirecting the run, which serves the transparency goal, and spin-off keeps threads focused. All three are cheap once forks exist.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (SRC) for rewind and spin-off; Claude desktop plus Codex (SRC) for side chat, with Codex's ephemeral read-only fork as the safest model
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 6 of 12 (side chat, common), 2 of 12 each (rewind, spin-off; differentiators)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Rewind: a checkpoint per user turn (conversation cursor plus artifact version ids); rewinding moves the cursor, restores versions and keeps the rewound tail recoverable until a new message is sent; a preview lists the per-artifact diffs that would be undone and warns about external effects. Side chat: an ephemeral child session seeded with a read-only snapshot of parent context, no effectful tools and no user prompts, not appended to the main transcript, stoppable independently, discarded or merged back as one message. Spin-off: a plan scope value or spawn_task tool creates a backlog chip with a self-contained prompt.

verevonToday.gap: Run checkpoints exist (SaveCheckpoint, auto-checkpoint compaction) but there is no user-facing rewind or restore. A grep for side chat in the chat feature found no hits, so there is no side-chat surface or ephemeral fork primitive. There is no user-facing spin-off or backlog; the nearest thing is wide-research fan-out inside Do runs.

items.approach: Rewind: move the active leaf of the R-t3-01-02 tree plus an artifact version pointer; scope per OD19 is conversation and artifact versions only, and effectful turns are marked non-rewindable with an explicit preview. Side chat: a model-gateway ephemeral invocation using the parent thread's assembled context snapshot (GetContextAssembly exists), the inline_tool_allowed read-only tool gate, no persistence under ZDR and an origin=side tag otherwise; SPA resizable side pane. Spin-off last: a spawn_task builtin that creates a draft thread in session-core.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (tree operations, ephemeral invocation), Frontend Plane (side pane, rewind preview)
items.risks: Users may assume rewind reverts external effects (emails, tickets), so the preview must be explicit. A second context costs tokens and must carry the parent's ACL and ZDR posture. Spin-off must never auto-start effectful work.

items.title: Resilient routing: failure vocabulary, credential pools, benching, usage-limit and refusal fallbacks, provider health
items.summary: Extend the shipped fallback chain in inference-core with a closed failure code set (auth, quota, rate limit, context too long, server, timeout, refusal, empty response) carrying retry_after, per-route retry policy, pooled deployments or credentials with model-scoped cooldowns, and benching of a failed primary until its declared reset. Add declared fallback models for usage-limit exhaustion with a switch-back at reset_at (opt-in when it crosses from a user subscription to platform billing), a policy-owned refusal fallback that records the original model and is undone on rewind or edit, and a per-provider health map exposed through ListModels so the picker greys unavailable routes with the reason.
items.whyItMatters: Fewer failed answers and stalled agent runs during provider incidents or quota exhaustion, which matters most for unattended scheduled agents and Azure deployment quotas. The subscription route currently stops at its limit with a typed message but no alternative.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: hermes (hermes-architecture-and-surfaces-095, 094 failover and credential pools); codexagent (036 usage-limit fallback and switch-back); claude (112 reversible refusal fallback); t3code (002, 050 provider health snapshot)
others: deepseek (126, 095 closed failure vocabulary and per-route retry modes)

items.whyItMatters: Serves the DeepSeek-style transparency goal, gives the router-policy page real data to tune Budget/Balance/Genius, and protects saved threads, agents and scheduled runs from provider model retirements. items.title: Editable permission rules, CEL policy and an MCP tool gate with consent receipts
items.summary: Add a rule store in capability-core (org, Space, user and thread scopes) over typed targets such as read_url(domain), send_mail(recipient) and command(prefix), resolved strictest-wins (deny > ask > ask-session > allow, with a wildcard allow surviving a merge only if both layers state it), so 'don't ask again' shows and edits the exact rule with its scope and org-scope rules are audited admin-gated changes. Optionally accept admin CEL expressions evaluated inside EvaluatePolicy (any deny wins, validated with dry-run), and when MCP tools are enabled add one execution-core gate that spends single-use consent receipts bound to the SHA-256 of the canonical arguments, reusing the approval descriptors.
items.whyItMatters: Editable 'don't ask again' rules are an acknowledged open item and the deterministic way to cut approval fatigue without an LLM in the permission path. Verevon already has the central decision point (capability-core EvaluatePolicy with signed Allow evidence and fail-closed unknown tools) that Claude is only now adding externally, and MCP is how users bring their own tools.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Antigravity (action(target) grant store with deny > ask > allow and per-conversation grants) with Claude (strictness lattice and strictest-wildcard folding, CEL rules and an external decision endpoint that fails closed, MCP gate with single-use consent receipts)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: declarative rules 2 of 12 (differentiator); CEL policy and MCP gate 1 of 12 each (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Rule = {action, target-pattern, effect deny|ask|ask_session|allow, scope, source}; exact match first, else fold the strictest over matching wildcards; deny from any scope wins; grants recorded per conversation. CEL rules {id, condition over (tool, args, session, user), action, reason}, any deny wins. MCP: wrap the transport, reject malformed frames and unlisted tools, mint a short-lived receipt (session, tool, sha256(canonical args)) on approval and execute only by spending a live matching receipt; reserve internal server-name prefixes.

verevonToday.gap: capability-core EvaluatePolicy returns Allow/Ask/Deny per capability with Ed25519-signed Allow evidence and the hook engine supports allow/deny/ask globs, but there is no user- or admin-authored rule set over typed targets, no ask-session level and editable don't-ask-again is not built. MCP tool names are denied by the inline loop (tool_loop.rs:625-645, verified) and execution-core rejects dynamic MCP names until capability-core provides a durable binding, so none of the MCP gating exists yet; nine capabilities sit in an unattested quarantine baseline.

items.approach: capability-core: rules table keyed by capability id plus target pattern with strictest-wins resolution in Go; execution-core passes the target (domain, recipient, path) in EvaluatePolicy and surfaces the matched rule and reason on denials and cards; SPA Rules settings page (reusing R-t3-11-02 scoped grants as the producer of rules). Optional cel-go rules per org inside EvaluatePolicy. MCP gate after capability-core issues per-tool capability ids: execution-core spends argument-hash receipts built on the existing exact-effect descriptors, with reserved server-name prefixes in capability-core.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Wildcard allows can silently widen authority: strictest-wins, audit every rule change and always show scope. Rule errors can lock users out, so validate and dry-run. Under master-ownership-matrix rule 12 an 'allow' rule for a provider write still needs a signed per-effect authorisation. MCP servers can return injected content, so combine with R-t3-11-07.

T3 Code (panel scope turn | branch | working tree, persisted per thread, stacked or split)
