items.title: One action-registry-driven command surface: palette, slash commands, shortcut sheet and safe double-Escape stop
items.summary: Build a Solid command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K) over the existing typed action registry, executing only low-risk reversible actions directly and opening the normal confirm dialog for the rest, with typed pickers for threads, projects and files and a content mode once server-side chat search lands. Move the fixed chat shortcuts into a declarative {command, key, when} table that renders a searchable Ctrl+/ sheet, add a double-Escape stop validated against the live run id and stream generation, and make the composer slash catalog and the palette read the same definitions.
items.whyItMatters: Power users and enterprise admins move faster, and the registry already carries zod I/O, owner plane, risk and reversibility, so palette actions are authority-checked for free. A safe keyboard stop for an agent run is also a trust feature.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: T3 Code (one palette reducer for commands, threads with content snippets, files and content search, with mutually exclusive modes; VS Code-style when-clauses, a key recorder and conflict flags) plus DeepSeek (searchable Mod+/ reference and a double-Escape stop bound to the live turn)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Palette: 4 of 12; keyboard-first and shortcuts: 6 of 12; slash commands: 3 of 12 (common to differentiator).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A palette state machine reduceCommandPaletteUiState(mode: command|files|content) where re-pressing the shortcut toggles closed and modes never stack; items {kind: action|submenu, searchTerms, threadContentMatch}. A declarative keybinding table {command, key, when} with per-OS overrides and a context-key evaluator. Stop requires two Escapes within a short window, each validated against {sessionId, turn, generation, focused region}. Slash commands come from one registry {name, description, inputHint, surfaces, handler}; a typed command never silently becomes a prompt.

verevonToday.gap: Ctrl/Cmd+K and bare "/" open global search but no palette executes actions (grep for CommandPalette and cmdk in src finds nothing). Chat has a handful of fixed shortcuts (new chat, focus composer, thread switch, Esc), no shortcut sheet, no rebinding and no double-Escape stop. A typed slash catalog does exist, but only in DashboardComposer: ComposerCommand entries with bilingual aliases, descriptions and argument hints, and an unknown /name is deliberately sent as plain text, the opposite of DeepSeek's guarantee, so that choice should be made deliberately. Whether the chat-page composer shares it was not verified. There is no server-side conversation search for a content mode.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: (1) extract a declarative shortcut table from use-chat-shortcuts.ts and render the Ctrl+/ sheet from it (task I1), testing nb-NO layouts for AltGr collisions; (2) add the double-Escape stop wired to the run id and stream generation; (3) build the palette as a Solid overlay over action-registry.ts, filtering by risk metadata so only low-risk reversible actions run directly; (4) lift the DashboardComposer command catalog into a shared module that both the slash menu and the palette consume, and decide the unknown-slash behaviour; (5) add the thread-content mode when full-text chat search lands (task I12). Defer user rebinding.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: The palette must not become a back door around approval gates, so reuse registry risk and reversibility metadata. Bare "/" already opens search outside the composer, so pick one meaning per context. Needs verification that the chat-page composer shares the slash catalog.

alreadyPlanned.where: Shortcut sheet is task I1 (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:215), full-text chat search is I12 (:222) and user slash command templates are I13 (:223). The palette itself and the double-Escape stop were not found in the plan.

items.title: Feedback surfaces and limit notices: shell toasts, composer banners, connection pill and role-aware limit messages
items.summary: Add a shell-level toast manager that outlives the panel that triggered it, a prioritised notice stack docked above the composer, and a connection pill driven by the chat stream state with hysteresis so healthy operation stays silent. Map the typed refusal codes and gateway 429s to inline notices that state the limit, the current value, the reset time and a role-aware action (member: ask your admin; owner: change plan or quota).
items.whyItMatters: Verevon spans many planes that fail independently, so calm, specific failure and limit feedback is a trust signal for an enterprise product. The typed refusal catalogue already exists, so the missing piece is the presentation layer.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: T3 Code (thread-scoped stacked toasts with expandable detail and copy-for-errors, composer banner stack) plus DeepSeek (toast vs in-place notice rule; connection pill with minimum-visible and recovered hold times) for feedback; Manus and Claude.ai (inline limit messages with reset, wait, upgrade or credits) for limits
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Feedback surfaces: 4 of 12; limit presentation: 4 of 12 (both common).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: One toast manager {threadRef, severity, detail, actions, copyable}; a composer banner stack with priority ordering; a connection indicator fed by the SSE/fetch layer that shows Reconnecting only after a short delay and holds Connected for about 2 s before hiding (DeepSeek, DOC); failed operations keep user data in place. Limits arrive as typed errors {limitKind, current, max, resetAt, actions[]} and map to inline notices with different calls to action for members and owners.

verevonToday.gap: Typed subscription, ZDR and capability refusal codes, org quotas and a 429 with Retry-After exist, and chat has reconnect handling in the live run panel with honest error events. The comparator's grep found no app-wide toast system (only ticket bulk actions) and no connection-status pill; how gateway 503 and 429 errors surface outside chat was not checked, so the feedback half is unknown. There is no live spend meter (task I16) and no inline notice of the form you hit X, resets at Y, ask your admin.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: add a toast manager and notice primitive in src/shared/ui, a ComposerNoticeStack in the chat composer, and a ConnectionPill fed by the chat-client stream state with an 800 ms minimum-visible and 2 s recovered hold. Map refusal codes (mp-contracts, model-gateway subscription_failure) and 429 responses to localised notices with role-aware actions. Model Plane cost-core exposes a per-run and per-month spend projection for the meter (task I16).
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Do not expose org spend to non-admin members. Avoid over-notifying: healthy stays silent. Needs verification of how non-chat pages surface gateway errors today and whether a toast primitive already exists under src/shared/ui.

items.title: Typed feature-flag and settings registry served by Control Plane, with kill switches and an agent-access class
items.summary: Replace the sprawl of per-crate environment flags with one typed registry (name, stage, default, owner, kill switch, agentAccess excluded|read|write) whose values are evaluated per org by Control Plane, cached in each service with a TTL and served to the SPA in the BFF boot payload. Fold the fragmented composer, org and profile settings into the same schema so one source feeds the settings UI and any future agent settings tool.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon has many built-but-dark features (Do on subscription, hooks, MCP dispatch, fine-tuning); today turning one on or off needs a redeploy and there is no per-org staging or record of what is live. An agent-access class is required before the agent can be given a settings tool.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop app
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: C-019: 4 of 12 (common). C-020: 5 of 12 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Flags: layered sources (static map, remote refresh, disk cache, fallback), exposure events, and staleness windows that disable security-sensitive features when flags are stale. Settings: a zod schema where each key carries scope, default and agent access (excluded, read, write); security-relevant keys are excluded from the agent's own settings tool, main-only keys cannot be set from the renderer, and grant maps can only be reduced.

verevonToday.gap: SRC: features are gated by ad hoc environment variables (AGENTIC_SUBSCRIPTION_ENABLED, the fine-tune feature env and separate env_flag helpers in execution-core and session-core) plus a capability promotion ledger TSV; there is no central typed registry, no per-org evaluation and no runtime kill switch. The only flag-like store in Control Plane is billing-core's per-plan feature_flags JSON map. Settings are spread across composer settings, BFF org settings and server-resolved profiles; the profile already lets clients only tighten posture, which is the right idea at the wrong breadth.

items.approach: Define a flag and settings schema crate in mp-contracts (name, stage dev|beta|stable|deprecated, default, owner, scope, agentAccess); Control Plane org-core serves per-org values (billing-core plan feature_flags can seed entitlement-driven flags); each service caches with TTL and fails closed for security gates when stale; the BFF boot payload exposes the SPA-visible subset; link flag state to the capability promotion ledger so a capability cannot be live without ledger evidence. Flags may only restrict: a flag must never widen ZDR or authority posture.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (registry), consumed by all planes
items.risks: Flag debt; a flag path that widens ZDR or authority would defeat the posture model; migration of existing settings rows.

items.title: Library of generated and uploaded files across chats, with org publishing built on Data Plane documents
items.summary: Register generated files and promoted artifacts (non-ZDR) as Data Plane v2 documents with origin_thread metadata, and build the library as a filtered document view with search, type grouping and favourites instead of a new store. 'Publish' is then 'save the artifact as a document and share it through the existing resource_grants and Application Plane collaboration', not a parallel publishing platform.
items.whyItMatters: Users want to find 'that report Verevon made last week' without hunting threads, and agentic products that produce deliverables converge on a library. Reusing Data Plane documents avoids duplicate storage and keeps sharing under existing grants.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (SRC) for the library; Claude desktop (SRC) for private-by-default published artifacts with roles
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 3 of 12 for the library (differentiator) and 3 of 12 for publishing (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A server file index keyed by owner with type, stage (process versus product), origin session, versions and share state; a library page with filters and batch download; storage quotas and recently-deleted restore (ChatGPT, DOC). Publishing: an artifact store with versions and an ACL (org, people, groups, email, public link; view, comment, edit), comments anchored to spots and @assistant comments routed to a watching session.

verevonToday.gap: No cross-chat file library: artifacts and generated files live per thread (partly client-side), and the Findings and Reports pages read the local transcript cache only. No artifact publishing, comments or runtime exist; the only sharing is document sharing through resource_grants in shares.rs, not chat artifacts.

items.approach: After R-t3-01-04, add a 'Save as document' action that creates a Data Plane v2 document with origin_thread metadata and reuses shares.rs and Control Plane grants for visibility. The library page is a filtered document view in the SPA. Comments and @assistant routing, if wanted, go through Application Plane collaboration rather than a new runtime. No durable library under ZDR.
items.planeOwner: Data Plane v2 (documents), Frontend Plane (library view), Control Plane (grants)
items.risks: Duplicated storage between session artifacts and documents; retention policy; public links conflict with ZDR and org data policies, so do not offer them by default.

items.title: Teach mode: record a user's hosted-browser workflow and distil it into a reviewed, replayable skill
items.summary: Record the steps a user performs in a Quarry-hosted browser session (including takeover sessions) as step receipts, have a Model Plane run draft a parameterised routine, send it through the skill proposal path for review, and replay it with per-step confirmation under the same evidence trail. Desktop recording stays out of scope.
items.whyItMatters: Learning by demonstration (Claude teach mode, Manus) is a differentiator (3 of 12) that fits Verevon's receipt machinery, but it depends on the browser, takeover and learning-governance work first.

items.title: Upgrade voice input: streaming dictation with a cleanup pass first, local speech-to-text for ZDR later, realtime delegation only if un-parked
items.summary: Phase 1: add a streaming speech endpoint in model-gateway (a proxied WebSocket, so provider keys never reach the browser and cost stays metered), capture with an AudioWorklet at 16 kHz PCM in about 40 ms frames, and one dictation state machine (idle, starting, listening, finishing, with a length cap) shared by the composer and voice mode, with an optional cleanup pass through the governed loop. Phase 2 (optional): local WASM speech-to-text in a worker with pinned model hashes for ZDR and temporary chat. Phase 3, only if the owner un-parks it: a realtime voice front end with exactly two tools (delegate and stay_silent) so every action stays in the governed loop.
items.whyItMatters: Dictation is table-stakes (6 of 11 sources) and exists, but one governed call per utterance feels slow and has no live text, and users on ZDR or in temporary chat have no voice input at all. A delegation-only realtime front end answers the governance concern behind the owner's park decision.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (SRC) and Antigravity (SRC) for streaming dictation; DeepSeek harness (SRC) for local speech-to-text; Codex (SRC) for governed realtime delegation
others: ChatGPT web (DOC, Live voice UX bar)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Dictation: 6 of 11 (5 distinct vendors), table-stakes. Realtime delegation: 2 of 11, differentiator. On-device speech-to-text: 1 of 11, unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Dictation: an AudioWorklet downsamples to 16 kHz PCM and posts about 40 ms frames; the page asks the backend for a short-lived speech credential or uses a backend WebSocket proxy; partial and final events return; a finishing state flushes; an optional cheap-model cleanup rewrites the final transcript using conversation context; a hard cap bounds session length. Local: lazy-download a quantised model (about 240 MB INT8) after explicit user preparation, verify size and SHA-256, run VAD plus recognition on the CPU, never send audio off the device. Realtime: WebRTC with a short-lived session secret; the realtime model has only delegate(text, mode new|steer|queue) and stay_silent, and delegate posts into the governed agent loop of the same thread; no spoken approvals.

verevonToday.gap: Dictation is shipped but is one governed call per utterance (record, upload, transcribe) with no live partials, no cleanup pass and an 8 MiB audio cap; no live microphone proof (DOC). Voice is refused under ZDR and blocked in temporary chat, so those users have no voice input. A realtime session mint exists (/v1/ai/realtime/session) but there is no browser WebRTC client; the bridge-core speech-LLM-speech pipeline is interfaces only; the owner parked duplex voice (OD19).

items.approach: Model Plane: a streaming speech route in model-gateway that proxies the provider WebSocket (cost and audit metered, ZDR refusal unchanged) or mints a short-lived scoped token; cleanup through the normal governed loop. Frontend Plane: AudioWorklet capture and the shared state machine in the composer and voice dialog; for phase 2 a worker running whisper.cpp or sherpa-onnx WASM with model files served from Verevon's CDN with pinned hashes, enabled only where the server path is refused, and tested on Norwegian audio. Phase 3 only after an owner ruling: the delegation endpoint calls the normal turn API, approvals stay on screen, and the realtime provider must be in an EU region with audio ZDR attested.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (model-gateway streaming proxy, realtime broker) with Frontend Plane (capture, state machine, local speech-to-text)
items.risks: Direct browser-to-provider streaming would bypass gateway metering unless proxied; ZDR must keep refusing server audio; Norwegian accuracy of small local models is unproven; realtime adds per-minute cost, EU-region latency and accidental spoken consent.

items.title: Run admission controls: credit-aware pause and resume, an org-level agent pause switch and clamped per-turn overrides
items.summary: Add a Control-plane org flag ("agents paused") checked at run, schedule and trigger admission and again at each continuation, as an incident-response kill switch (drain.rs only handles redeploys today). Add a paused_for_credit run status when the cost reservation fails mid-run (persist state, resume on a billing event, and show queue position or a cheaper tier at admission). Add a typed per-turn override envelope (model, effort, approval posture) validated and clamped server-side against Control-plane entitlements.
items.whyItMatters: Long agent runs, goals and schedules make admission control matter: enterprise admins need a fast stop, and a run should pause rather than die at a credit boundary. Per-turn overrides let users move a hard step to a stronger model without losing context. All three are cheap once runs are resumable.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (install-wide pause through a fail-safe sentinel) for the kill switch; Perplexity (pauses rather than cancels on credit exhaustion) for credit pause; Codex (typed 27-field TurnStartParams) for overrides
others: Manus (per-tier wait estimates, idleness reporting and maintenance fence)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: emergency stop 2 of 12; credit-aware admission 2 of 12 (differentiator); per-turn overrides 4 of 12 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A global or org pause flag is checked at admission for runs, schedules and triggers. Before each round check the cost reservation; on shortfall set paused_for_credit and persist state, and a billing event resumes the run. A typed TurnStart{model, effort, approval_policy, ...} is validated server-side and clamped per surface and plan.

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/drain.rs:1-20 and 103 (graceful drain on redeploy with /readyz 503 and in-flight completion)

No baseline record for org-level pause, credit-aware pause or a typed per-turn override envelope; cost reservation (proposal section 18) is listed as not built per the cluster; normalize.rs not re-read
verevonToday.gap: Drain on redeploy exists. No org-level or global pause of new agent work was found, no paused_for_credit state, and whether Do runs accept a typed per-turn model or effort override clamped by entitlements was not verified.

items.approach: Control Plane org setting plus Model Plane admission. Gateway and capability-core read the org flag at run, schedule and trigger admission; cost-core reservation failure transitions the run to paused_for_credit via the continuation machinery; extend the invoke contract with typed per-turn overrides clamped by Control-plane entitlements.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (flag, entitlements) with Model Plane (admission)
items.risks: Billing correctness around pause and resume; entitlement bypass if overrides are not clamped server-side; the policy for an unreadable pause flag (fail open or fail closed) must be an explicit, documented choice.

items.title: Per-Space environment specs and prebuilt sandbox images
items.summary: Let a Space or org define a sandbox environment declaratively (base image, setup script, env with secret refs, network policy, named actions) and prebuild it into a content-hashed image that is rebuilt on spec change or on a schedule, so agent sandboxes start fast on a healthy, reproducible base.
items.whyItMatters: Enterprise customers and Spaces can preinstall their tools and connectors, so agent runs skip install time and behave reproducibly. Without it every run pays setup cost or works with a fixed package set.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude (cloud environments with setup script, env vars and network policy, vendor or self-hosted) plus Cursor (prebuilt images with recurring rebuilds, build logs and health tracking)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 12 sources (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A spec {base_image, setup_script, env (secret refs), network_policy, actions[]} is stored per org or Space; a builder runs it in a fresh VM and snapshots the result as an image with a content hash and logs; sandboxes boot from the latest healthy image; a rebuild runs on spec change or cron.

verevonToday.gap: code_interpreter runs in a fixed image with a fixed package set. There is no per-org or per-Space environment definition, no setup script and no image build pipeline.

items.approach: Model Plane: sandbox-manager (Go) owns the environment spec per Space; image builds run as durable workflows in orchestrator-core (it already hosts Temporal activities); secrets are referenced by id and resolved by the item 7 injection proxy, never baked into images; build logs and health are shown in the Space settings UI.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (sandbox-manager, orchestrator-core)
items.risks: Supply-chain risk in setup scripts, image storage cost, and secrets leaking into images.

items.title: Sandbox computer extensions: persistent machine mode, execution-target picker, authenticated dev-server preview
items.summary: Once the sandbox computer exists, add a persistent flag on a lease that keeps its disk (installed tools, services, databases), a device_ref on runs so a task can move between an ephemeral sandbox and a persistent machine, and an authenticated preview URL per listening port that opens in the Quarry hosted browser so the agent can verify what it built.
items.whyItMatters: Teams that automate recurring work with installed software need a machine that survives between runs (and it is a revenue line), and agents that build small apps or dashboards need to preview and verify them. Value is moderate for an AI workspace and depends on item 3.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (always-on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS cloud computers with chosen compute and region; one active-device concept that tasks can move between) plus Claude (preview auto-verify, element selection, port discovery) plus Cursor (port forwarding from cloud VMs into shareable previews)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 12 for persistent computers, 2 of 12 for device switching, 4 of 12 for dev-server preview
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A long-lived VM with a persistent disk and a guest agent, billed monthly, backed up as disk snapshots. Task.device_ref {kind: sandbox | cloud_computer, id} resolves the host through the backend trait; switching rehydrates the workspace and re-runs from the last checkpoint. Preview: detect listening ports, probe HTML, expose through an authenticated proxy shown in the hosted browser surface.

verevonToday.gap: Files persist per Space through the CAS workspace, which covers the most common persistence need without paying for idle machines, but there is no persistent machine, no user-visible target choice (one implicit execution-core target and a Space-scoped lease), and no way to preview a server the agent runs: HTML artifacts render in a sandboxed srcdoc iframe only.

items.approach: sandbox-manager: a persistent flag on the item 3 lease that retains the VM disk, billed through cost-core; session-core adds device_ref on runs and the composer gets a picker; sandbox-manager issues an authenticated preview URL per port that Quarry's hosted browser opens (the Model proposes, Quarry executes). Require auth on every preview and apply Space ACLs.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (sandbox-manager, session-core)
items.risks: Cost, abuse and data residency for persistent machines; public exposure of previews unless authenticated; partial-state confusion when moving a task mid-flight. Low confidence on demand for the picker.

items.title: Review as a run: read-only reviewer subagent with strict P0-P3 findings, merged with the deterministic source checks
items.summary: Add a 'review this' run for an artifact revision, a workspace turn diff or attached files. A read-only reviewer subagent returns findings in a validated schema (title, body, priority P0-P3, confidence, location, plus overall correctness) and may report nothing. Deterministic findings from source_validation.rs are merged into the same schema and card, and 'apply fix' sends a finding back as a scoped edit turn.
items.whyItMatters: A trustworthy, located second pass is useful for code, reports and contracts alike, and four of nine references ship a review run. Verevon already has a rare strength here (deterministic checks of numbers, dates, word counts and revision preservation against sources); putting both reviewers behind one findings card makes that strength visible and consistent.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (review/start with four targets, inline or detached delivery, steering disabled during review, strict findings JSON and a 'report only what the author would fix' standard)
others: Claude desktop (best findings-card UX: walkthrough, apply fix, rerun)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 9 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: review/start {target, delivery, threadId} spawns a read-only sandboxed reviewer with a target-specific prompt (uncommitted changes, merge-base diff, a commit, or custom instructions). Output is held to a schema {findings[{title, body, confidence_score, priority, code_location}], overall_correctness, overall_confidence_score}; an explicit-only review skill enforces 'no invented findings'. The UI renders a findings card and 'apply fix' sends a finding back as a scoped edit turn.

verevonToday.gap: There is no code or generic review run and no findings card. The existing source-bound review is automatic, document-only and reports inside the drafting flow rather than as a user-invokable, located, prioritised review. Subagents exist (subagent.* tools are bound to cap.agent.spawn) but there is no review profile.

items.approach: Model Plane: a review subagent profile with a read-only capability set (fs.read, fs.grep, read_artifact; no edit or process tools) and a findings JSON schema enforced through the structured-output path; drop findings without a location or below a confidence threshold. Targets: artifact revision diff, Space workspace turn diff (R-t3-07-03), attached code or documents. Map deterministic source_validation findings into the same schema as high-confidence items. Frontend Plane: a findings card with priority chips and 'apply fix', which sends a scoped revision turn: for artifacts through the selection-bound range splice in R-t3-07-05, for workspace files through R-t3-07-01's fs.edit.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (model-gateway, execution-core) with Frontend Plane for the card
items.risks: False positives erode trust: enforce the 'only what the author would fix' standard, a confidence floor and a reviewer that cannot write. Reviewer cost doubles the work on big diffs, so make it explicit-only and budgeted. Keep deterministic and model findings visibly distinct.

items.title: Multi-file app build and preview: static web bundles first, built output next, screenshots through Quarry
items.summary: Let agents ship a small multi-file web app or dashboard safely. Phase 0: a multi-file static bundle artifact (HTML plus CSS/JS files, no build) rendered in the existing sandboxed iframe. Phase 1: build inside the Space sandbox with a pinned, pre-baked toolchain and serve the dist output from a per-run isolated origin through the Frontend gateway. Phase 2: dev-server ports and authenticated previews, which belong to R-t3-06-10. UI screenshots of the preview are taken through Quarry.
items.whyItMatters: 'Build me a small app or dashboard' is a headline use case for claude.ai, ChatGPT and Manus, and Verevon's agents can only produce single-file HTML. A safe preview extends an existing strength (sandboxed HTML artifacts) to multi-file outputs and closes a visible gap against the references.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (dev-server candidate detection, explanations for cold starts and port conflicts, request throttling, ask-Claude fallback)
others: Manus (checkpoint previews and webdev LSP presets)
ChatGPT web (preview of built apps, DOC)
Claude.ai web (artifacts shared between code and chat, DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 9 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: The workspace declares a start command and port, or the agent detects them, and the sandbox runs it. A reverse proxy exposes the port to a sandboxed iframe on a per-run origin. Checkpoints snapshot the workspace and serve a static build for comparison, and a screenshot tool captures the preview for the model.

verevonToday.gap: Single-file HTML artifacts render in an iframe with sandbox=allow-scripts and no same-origin, with a version stepper. The artifact kinds are code, document, html, spreadsheet, file and image, so there is no multi-file project kind. The Space sandbox has no network and no port exposure (process_start: 'NO NETWORK, read-only system'), and there is no build step, dev-server preview or screenshot-of-preview loop.

items.approach: Phase 0 (INF, no new infrastructure): a bundle artifact kind carrying a files map, composed into one srcdoc (or blob URLs) for the existing sandboxed iframe, with the no-same-origin rule unchanged. Phase 1: execution-core builds the leased workspace with a pinned toolchain from a pre-baked image (R-t3-06-08), since the sandbox cannot install dependencies, then publishes the dist folder to a per-run isolated origin served by the Rust gateway with a strict CSP and no cookies. Phase 2: hand over to R-t3-06-10 for ports and authenticated preview URLs. Screenshots of any preview go through Quarry (the Model proposes, Quarry executes), never a Model Plane browser.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (execution-core, sandbox-manager) with Frontend Plane gateway for the preview origin
items.risks: Serving untrusted code needs strict per-run origins, a CSP and no cookies; keep allow-same-origin out. ZDR runs must not persist builds beyond the lease. A networkless build only works for projects whose dependencies are vendored or pre-baked, which limits what 'build' can mean at first.

items.title: Code edit quality on demand: post-write diagnostics (decision H11) and an optional apply_patch format where a provider benefits

items.whyItMatters: Cursor's shadow lints and Codex's grammar-constrained patches matter for coding products; for Verevon (not an IDE) they are conditional optimisations once file tools exist.

items.title: Use Verevon from other agents and work tools: outward MCP endpoint and channel adapters
items.summary: Host an MCP server over the typed action registry (Streamable HTTP with OAuth) so users can reach Verevon from Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor, and let Quarry consume WebMCP site tools as proposals that the Model Plane may select and Quarry executes. Separately, build Slack, Teams and email entry points as channel adapters in the future Channel Plane, with identity binding, per-channel routing, progress mirrored back and a consent card stating who posts as whom.
items.whyItMatters: It grows usage by meeting users where they already work (channel entry points 5 of 12 sources; outward MCP or WebMCP 3 of 12). It is a later phase because it depends on the action registry being open to agents (item 05) and on a Channel Plane ADR.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Hermes (mcp serve exposes conversations as MCP tools; SRC) plus ChatGPT web (consumes WebMCP site tools whose instructions cannot authorise sensitive actions; DOC) for outward interop; Cursor (Slack, Linear, GitHub and Teams start cloud agents with routing rules and mirrored progress; SRC) with Claude desktop (a session bound to a Slack thread through a disclosure-bearing consent card; SRC) for channels
others: Manus and Manus web (email and IM channels)

Channels: adapters (webhook or events API) -> identity binding (channel user to platform user) -> routing rule -> run creation with the channel as origin -> progress and result posted back, with a consent card naming channel, workspace and posting identity.

Channel adapters wait for the Channel Plane ADR and live in that plane, not in Model Plane; identity binding is Control-owned; Application Plane holds routing projections.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (MCP endpoint) with Ingestion Plane/Quarry (WebMCP) and the future Channel Plane (adapters)
items.risks: External agents acting with user tokens; identity-binding errors post private data to shared channels; ZDR must propagate to outward calls; the WebMCP evidence is DOC and low confidence.

items.title: Time-based media on demand: transcribe recordings into documents, pull meeting minutes, and expose video generation and understanding
items.summary: Four optional capabilities on one pipeline, to schedule on demand. (1) Audio and video uploads become transcript documents: chunk by silence, transcribe with the existing governed speech-to-text, store a Data Plane document with a back-reference to the media. (2) Meeting minutes from Teams or Zoom transcripts pulled through integration-corev2 with no recording, summarised in the Model Plane, with action items written through governed actions. (3) Expose the existing Sora job API as an async video_generate tool behind a cost-confirmation approval. (4) Video understanding through a Gemini route behind capability gating.
items.whyItMatters: Meeting recordings, voice notes and training clips would become searchable knowledge and tasks, and marketing teams ask for video. All four are off the critical chat and agent path, need new providers or connectors, and rest mostly on documentation, so they follow the priority and recommended set.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Perplexity web (DOC) for transcribed audio and video with speakers; ChatGPT Meetings (DOC) for the privacy design (no bot, private by default, audio deleted after notes); Manus (SRC) for video modes and a cost confirmation; Antigravity (SRC) for the typed media part
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Meetings 3 of 11 and video generation 3 of 11 (each 2 distinct vendors), common; audio and video uploads 2 of 11 (DOC only), video understanding 2 of 11, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Uploads: object storage, transcode to 16 kHz mono, chunk by silence under the speech-to-text limit, transcribe with diarisation, stitch with timestamps, store the transcript as a document linked to the media and index it. Meetings: native recorder or platform connector, then transcript, summary with action items, then a page with linked tasks; raw audio deleted after processing. Video generation: async job tool video_generate{prompt, start_image?, ratio, length, quality} with an approval card that shows cost per quality tier. Video understanding: a typed media part {mime_type, blobref, duration_seconds, thumbnail} routed to a video-capable model or subagent.

items.approach: First check imports-core and the doc_indexed_consumer for audio MIME handling and transcript documents. Then Data Plane ingestion calls Model Plane speech-to-text per chunk (Data Plane owns orchestration and storage, Model Plane owns inference), with ZDR orgs refused persistence. Meetings: integration-corev2 transcript connectors for Teams and Zoom, summarisation in the Model Plane, tasks through governed actions. Video: expose the Sora job as an async tool with a cost-confirmation approval and a video artifact renderer in the Output panel; add a Gemini provider in inference-core before a video_analyze subagent that takes a Data Plane attachment id and is gated by R-t3-02-03.
items.planeOwner: Data Plane (transcript documents) with Model Plane (speech, video tools), Ingestion Plane (meeting connectors) and Frontend Plane (video artifact)
items.risks: Cost of long audio and of video generation; personal data in recordings (consent, retention, recording law); video-provider availability and residency in the EU; speaker identification is unreliable (ChatGPT documents this).

(2) Adopt Microsoft sensitivity-label checks in Data Plane document access through integration-corev2 Graph metadata, with allow and deny effects; Office add-ins themselves stay deferred.

others: ChatGPT web (DOC, broader add-in coverage including Google Sheets)

items.title: Tighten-only runtime monitors: asynchronous action reviewer and information-flow control
items.summary: If the owners revisit the standing 'no LLM on the permission path' ruling for a restricted role, add an asynchronous reviewer between capability policy and the human card that can only deny or escalate and never grant, fed user turns plus the proposed tool call and never tool outputs, using a versioned rule set (must-name intent-clearing rules, agent-authored argument provenance, deterministic forced-card checks) and failing closed to a human card. Separately, add admin-defined data classification on threads and connectors with session taint and approval on downward flows, built from the existing restricted-context write block and privacy tiers.
items.whyItMatters: A trajectory monitor is a second line of defence against injection-driven actions in Do-mode, and classification-aware flow control stops confidential Data Plane content leaking to Slack or email through agents. Neither is needed to make approvals usable: that is delivered deterministically by R-t3-11-02, -03 and -04. The comparator rated the reviewer priority (7 of 12 sources) but Verevon's architecture rules exclude the approval-granting form, so it is re-tiered here.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex Guardian v2 (asynchronous trajectory scoring with thresholds, gating later actions, fail closed) plus Claude (classifier policy discipline: must-name rules, tool-result blindness, forceAsk escalations) for the reviewer; Manus (admin classification levels, per-connector input and output levels, approval on downward flow) for flow control
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: auto-review 7 of 12 (table-stakes elsewhere); classifier policy text 1 of 12 (unique); flow control 3 of 12 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Reviewer gets user messages plus proposed tool name and arguments (not tool outputs) and a policy prompt, returns {decision, reason, risk 0..1}; allow below a threshold, escalate above it, deny on clear violation; N consecutive denials pause the run; reviewer failure fails closed to a human card; every verdict is logged. Flow control: ordered levels, a session level that rises when it reads higher-classified data, connector max input levels, writes above the destination level need approval or are blocked, downgrades explicit and audited.

verevonToday.gap: No reviewer model exists; risk is a coarse substring classifier. The repo has a standing decision against LLM-on-the-permission-hot-path (HAP WS-3, CHD 13.3 anti-pattern) and ownership-matrix rule 12 says effectful calls need a signed durable authorisation, so an LLM auto-approve tier is excluded. Flow control is partial: a consent-to-disclose predicate, a restricted-context write block and privacy-tier routing exist, but no admin-defined classification with session taint.

items.approach: execution-core: Reviewer step after EvaluatePolicy using a cheap inference-core route; the verdict can only lower Allow to Ask or Deny, consecutive denials pause the run, verdicts go to the run trace and audit outbox, ZDR runs use a ZDR-attested reviewer or force a human, and NeverAuto and hard floors stay outside the classifier. Policy text is versioned data in capability-core with red-team fixtures. Flow control: Data Plane labels documents, Model Plane raises a thread's level on retrieval, capability-core stores connector levels, execution-core checks before provider writes and routes to HITL with an explicit audited downgrade.
dependencies: ADR: LLM on the permission path (HAP WS-3, rule 12)
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (reviewer, taint checks); Data Plane (document labels); Control Plane (classification levels)
items.risks: Conflicts with the standing decision if it ever grants; keep it tighten-only and asynchronous. Classifier false negatives under injection and policy drift from tool semantics. Taint over-propagation makes threads unusable, so provide a reviewed downgrade.

items.title: Reader and appearance polish: conversation TOC and chapters, font size and dyslexia-friendly font, org accent and environment identity, calm tips, reasoning translation
items.summary: A floating table of contents from user messages and headings; user font, density and dyslexia-font preferences; an organisation accent generated for safe contrast and an admin banner; an environment pill; a calm tip registry; and opt-in, cost-isolated translation of model reasoning that is never fed back to the model.
items.whyItMatters: Theming is widespread (7 of 12) and accessibility preferences matter, but these are polish items with modest benefit; Verevon's accessibility baseline (live regions, accessible charts, focus rings) is already strong.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (SRC) for chapters, TOC and appearance settings; T3 Code (SRC) for collapsing long prompts; DeepSeek harness (SRC) for reasoning translation ; T3 Code (about 56 colour roles, an OKLCH generator that solves contrast, independent font families and sizes, build-stage artwork) plus Claude desktop (admin org banner and deployment identity, tip registry with shown, clicked and dismissed tracking, What's New modal)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-01-15: 2 of 12 sources each; differentiators | R-t3-12-12: Theming: 7 of 12 (table-stakes, Verevon has the basic form); environment identity: 2 of 12; tips and What's New: 1 of 12.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A mark_chapter tool inserts a titled divider and the UI builds a floating TOC from chapters (or from headings once a conversation exceeds roughly five responses). Semantic colour roles as CSS custom properties with separate light and dark themes;

verevonToday.gap: R-t3-01-15: No chapters or TOC (grep found none). | R-t3-12-12: Theme toggle only: no accent, density, font-size or dyslexia-font preference;

items.approach: CSS-variable preferences first; TOC after render performance work.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane with optional Control Plane branding
items.risks: Low. Translation must not touch ZDR turns through a retained path.

dropped.reason: Local execution host companion is explicitly parked by the owner and only applies to desktop/IDE products; Verevon is a cloud web product whose execution belongs in the per-thread sandbox computer (F-t3-009). Revisit only if user-desktop control is unparked by ADR.

Best-of-N parallel workspace attempts come from one IDE source (Cursor), conflict with the 2026-08-24 decision-ledger ruling against workspace isolation for parallel agents, and Verevon is not an IDE; multi-model comparison for answers is covered by the Model Council nice-to-have (F-t3-092).

waves.goal: Make what already exists trustworthy and correct: one run context for Do runs, durable and multi-replica-safe runs, declared tool risk with MCP callable, audit delivery, ZDR live, learning and memory governance, cache and cost basics, render performance, release and CI guardrails.

Close the agent-loop and governance gaps users feel in chat and Do mode: approvals v2, plan-continue and ask_user, working connectors and agent browser, history foundation, Spaces as projects, verified Office deliverables, scheduled Do runs, the attention model, file tools, the action registry for agents and the org policy registry; start the sandbox-computer seam.

Deliver the research, creation and personalisation table-stakes on top: deep and wide research, citations to passages, readable long runs, artifact canvas, decks, Agents and Automations hubs, takeover, goals, skills lifecycle, scoped memory and personalisation, model record and Gemini, eval gates, egress tiers and the microVM sandbox.

Become a computer-using platform: computer use in the sandbox desktop, the live computer panel, inline widgets and MCP Apps on a user-content origin, sharing, event triggers, replay, images, custom connectors, plugins, public Agent API and bring-your-own providers.
Nice-to-have backlog, scheduled on demand or when a dependency makes them cheap.

adrNeeded.topic: Sandbox computer backend and thread-scoped workspace (microVM per thread, snapshot retention and destruction, cost metering)
adrNeeded.why: Moves execution from hermetic per-call bwrap processes to long-lived machines and introduces durable state outside Spaces; must show ZDR snapshot destruction, that a thread workspace never bypasses Space ACLs, supply-chain ownership of guest images, and VM-second billing.

adrNeeded.topic: Computer-use scope: desktop control only inside Verevon's sandbox VM; user-desktop control stays parked
adrNeeded.why: The owner parked OS-level desktop control; the Endpoint Plane can capture and inject input on real machines. An ADR should fix the boundary (sandbox only, consent tiers if ever unparked) and keep the 'Model proposes, executor executes' rule for desktop actions.

adrNeeded.topic: Spaces as the chat project container, instruction precedence and multi-author authority (OD19)
adrNeeded.why: Projects must not become a second container beside Spaces; precedence between org, Space, project and persona instructions, and whose delegated token runs a collaborator-triggered agent turn, need a ruling so Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL.

adrNeeded.topic: Agent-browser domain policy ownership and model-blind credentials (OD13)
adrNeeded.why: Decides whether broker, Control or Quarry owns the domain fence and per-site read/act consent, and how vault secrets are substituted by Quarry so the Model never sees them, preserving 'the Model proposes browser actions and Quarry executes or rejects them'.

adrNeeded.topic: Unattended authority: scheduled, goal and trigger runs, stored consent with expiry, renewable delegated credentials (owner ruling 2026-09-28, OD8, D10)
adrNeeded.why: Today scheduled runs are draft-only by owner ruling and the delegated bearer lives 300 s. Tool-using unattended runs need a signed, expiring consent contract, a non-delegable set and a renewal path through Control, not a service-principal shortcut.

adrNeeded.topic: Share model, public links and artifact hosting origin under ZDR and residency
adrNeeded.why: Public snapshots, published artifacts and a dedicated user-content origin create new egress and retention paths; connectors called from a shared artifact must run with the viewer's credentials. Must state which content types (ZDR threads, private connector content) can never be shared.

adrNeeded.topic: Learned and distributed behaviour: three-tier skill library (vendor, org, user), promotion gate and plugin supply chain
adrNeeded.why: The promotion gate is deliberately unbuilt pending a product decision while the loop already writes org-matchable skills; executable skill and plugin bundles add code supply-chain risk. One ADR should define scopes, approval, pinning and kill lists.

adrNeeded.topic: Model entitlements and provider credentials ownership (allowed_models has no owner; BYO keys custody)
adrNeeded.why: model-gateway refuses the OrgPolicy allowed_models field because no service owns it. Control Plane should decide and Model Plane enforce; bring-your-own provider keys must stay in Integration Core custody with ZDR and residency attestation per connection.

adrNeeded.topic: LLM reviewers on the permission path (revisit HAP WS-3 and ownership-matrix rule 12 for tighten-only monitors)
adrNeeded.why: Codex-style guardian reviewers conflict with the standing 'no LLM on the permission hot path' decision; only a tighten-only (deny or escalate, never grant) design could be compatible and needs an explicit ruling.

adrNeeded.topic: Connector content in shared Spaces and ZDR propagation for connector and web reads
adrNeeded.why: Personal mailbox and drive content read by an agent in a Space thread must not become visible to other members, and ZDR must propagate to connector reads, citations and research ledgers.
